{{Short description|Quartic plane curve}}
[[File:Bullet nose curve.svg|thumb|right|226px|Bullet-nose curve with {{math|1=''a'' = 1}} and {{math|1=''b'' = 1}}]]

In [[mathematics]], a '''bullet-nose curve''' is a [[unicursal curve | unicursal]] quartic curve with three [[inflection point]]s, given by the equation
:<math>a^2y^2-b^2x^2=x^2y^2 \,</math><ref>{{Cite web |last=Weisstein |first=Eric W. |title=Bullet Nose |url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/BulletNose.html |access-date=2026-02-13 |website=mathworld.wolfram.com |language=en}}</ref>

The bullet curve has three [[double point]]s in the [[real projective plane]], at {{math|1=''x'' = 0}} and {{math|1=''y'' = 0}}, {{math|1=''x'' = 0}} and {{math|1=''z'' = 0}}, and {{math|1=''y'' = 0}} and {{math|1=''z'' = 0}}, and is therefore a unicursal (rational) curve of [[geometric genus|genus]] zero.

If 
:<math>f(z) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} {2n \choose n} z^{2n+1} = z+2z^3+6z^5+20z^7+\cdots</math>
then
:<math>y = f\left(\frac{x}{2a}\right)\pm 2b\ </math>
are the two branches of the bullet curve at the origin.
